title: Counting allocations
description:
Replace global `operator new` and `delete` to count every allocation.

```
before: 0 live allocations
vector of 1000 ints: 11 allocations, 1 live
string "short": 0 allocations (small string optimisation)
after everything: 0 live, peak 7,936 bytes
```
hints: Defining `operator new(std::size_t)` and `operator delete(void*)` at global scope **replaces** the library's versions: from then on every `new` and `delete` in the program, including the ones inside `std::vector` and `std::string`, calls yours. The compiler may also call the sized form, `void operator delete(void* p, std::size_t size) noexcept`; define it to call your plain `operator delete(p)` so both paths are counted.
To track bytes, store the size in a small header before the block you return, and read it back in `delete`, the same trick the real allocator uses (lesson 4.03).
Do not use `std::cout` inside `operator new`: printing may allocate and call it again.
requirements: Replace `operator new(std::size_t)` and `operator delete(void*) noexcept` (and the sized delete) with versions that call `std::malloc`/`std::free` and update counters.
Report allocations, live blocks and the peak bytes in use.
Use the counters to show where a leak is.
stretch: Record the size of each live block in a fixed array to print the biggest ones.
